chunks: And Muhammad ibn al-Hasan narrated to me from Muhammad ibn al-Hasan al-Saffar, from Ahmad ibn Muhammad ibn Isa, from his father, from Ibn Abi Umayr, from Hisham ibn al-Hakam, from Abd al-Karim ibn Hassan, who said:

I asked Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him): 'What is meant by the saying that the Ziyarah of the grave of al-Husayn (peace be upon him) equals one Hajj and one Umrah?' He replied: 'Verily, the Hajj and Umrah are here (in Makkah). And if a man intended to perform Hajj but was not able to do so, and he went (to the grave), Allah would record for him one Hajj. And if a man intended to perform Umrah but was not able to do so, one Umrah would be recorded for him.'
ai.seo_question: What is the spiritual reward of visiting the grave of Imam al-Husayn compared to Hajj and Umrah?
ai.summary: Imam al-Sadiq (peace be upon him) clarifies that the ziyarah of Imam al-Husayn (peace be upon him) serves as a substitute for Hajj and Umrah specifically for those who intended to perform these rituals but were prevented by circumstances, thereby earning the full reward. This hadith highlights the concept of *ta'wil* (spiritual equivalence) in Shia jurisprudence, where the spiritual merit of the Ahl al-Bayt's shrines can compensate for the physical absence from the Kaaba, emphasizing that intention (*niyyah*) and capability are key factors in this divine concession.
